newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria bomb kills five, hurts 15 in garrison town.
newsitem.headline: Algeria bomb kills five, hurts 15 in garrison town.

text.p: A car bomb explosion killed five people and wounded 15 on Sunday in the Algerian garrison town of Blida near Algiers, Algerian security forces said.

The blast, four days before Algerians vote on changing the constitution, jolted Blida at about 9.20 a.m. (0820 GMT), said a statement from the security forces carried by the official Algerian news agenct APS.
Residents, speaking by telephone from Blida, said the bomb went off outside a hotel where police officers usually reside.
"The five killed people were three men, a women and a girl, all killed as they were passing by," one resident said.

The targeted hotel in downtown Blida was slightly damaged, said another resident. "The hotel was heavily protected by concrete blocks all around to prevent such a bomb attack," said the resident, who lives nearby.
Some neighbouring houses were also slightly damaged by fragments flying from the explosion, she said.
The explosion, the last in a spate of car bombings in Blida and other towns elsewhere in Algeria during the past three years, went off at the centre of Blida known as Sahat Attout, residents said.
The military headquarters for Algiers and neighbouring towns are located in Bilda, 50 km (30 miles) south of the capital.

The bomb attack followed a series of raids and mass killing of civilians which the Algerian authorities blame on Moslem rebels waging a five-year-old guerrilla struggle against the North African state.
More than 120 people, including children and women, have been killed in the past six weeks, according to independent sources in Algiers.

Algerian daily Liberte said on Sunday Moslem guerrillas detonated a home-made bomb on Saturday underneath a railway line in the western province of Sidi Bel Abbes, some 400 km (250 km) west of Algiers.
The explosion occurred just before the train, carrying workers to the neighbouring oil and gas hub Oran, crossed the blasted section of the line. There were no casualties, said Liberte.
Algerian newspapers have dubbed the month leading to the November 28 referendum as the "Month of all horrors".
The draft constitution bans politicians from using Islam, among other things, as a weapon to gain power.
